title: Sweeten a glass of tea with sugar from a jar and stir it
household_need: Sweeten a glass of tea by pouring sugar straight from the jar: too little and it is not sweet, too much and it is sickly; the pour has to stop by eye while the sugar piles up on the bottom.
instruction: Add 10 to 25 g of sugar from the open jar to the glass of tea. Sugar runs once the jar tilts past 40-60 degrees (later when emptier), faster with more tilt (max 4 g/s), and settles as a white mound: 10 g is 5.2 cm across, 25 g 7.0 cm. 2 g spilled outside the glass fails. Set the jar down upright and let go. Then stir two full clockwise turns (seen from above), the spoon's whole head under the surface, and put the spoon back in its basket, released. No stirring until the jar is down.
core_interventions: left arm: pick up the open sugar jar, tilt it over the glass, stop the pour in the gram band, set the jar down upright and release it
right arm: once the jar is down, stir two net clockwise turns and release the spoon in the basket

process.state: grams of sugar in the glass m (and in the jar, and in the air)
process.model: q = 4 g/s x c x min(1, (theta - theta0) / 35 deg)^1.5 while the jar tilt theta exceeds theta0 = 30 + 80 x (1 - jar sugar / 94 g) deg; sugar leaving the mouth lands with a 0.12 s time constant, in the glass if the stream from the jar's lowest mouth point falls inside the glass mouth, else spilled

hidden.jar_sugar_g: U[60, 85] g at the start (onset tilt 38-59 deg)

nominal.note: band per tier chosen by the user (2026-11-19); the pour is the same at every tier (time_scale unused). At the fastest hidden flow and full tilt the hard band lasts 5 / 4.6 = 1.09 s (1 s floor of the time-limit rule); easy 4.3 s, medium 3.3 s

process.cue: sugar mound on the glass bottom (cone at the 33 deg slope of settled sugar, sized from the grams: 10 g 5.2 cm, 15 g 5.9 cm, 25 g 7.0 cm, 30 g 7.5 cm across; the bottom is 7.7 cm), seen through the clear tea from the head camera; the falling stream; the sugar left in the glass jar. Stirring dissolves the mound (appearance only)

timing.event: the jar set down upright and released (>= 1 s): the grams in the glass then are judged
timing.rule: quality 1 inside the tier's band; linear penalty to 0 at 5 g and at 10 g above the band

physical: jar released upright (< 10 deg) and supported on the counter >= 1 s
spoon head stayed in the glass, under the tea, during 2 net clockwise turns
stirring only after the jar is down
spoon released, supported in basket, low speed >= 1 s
completion.temporal: grams in the glass at the set-down inside the tier's band

failures: jar, spoon or glass dropped or the jar left lying
stirring before the jar is down
permitted: pre-grasping the spoon while the sugar pours
prohibited: taking sugar back out of the glass
arm_roles: left: sugar jar; right: spoon (dual-arm by user design)
demo_guidance: Physics overlay and oracle: src/roboclock/envs/household/a1_x5/sim.py. The left arm pinches the jar body 3.5 cm up (tool azimuth 45 deg, 10 deg down; reach-screened, >= 0.27 rad joint margin), carries it upright beside the glass and tilts it toward +x while the mouth moves over the glass.
The tilt rises at 45 deg/s to the first flow, is servoed to 2.5 g/s and tips back once glass + air + 0.3 s of flow reach the middle of the band (privileged task grams).
The right arm's spoon routine is the tea-infuser version's, gated on the jar being released.
open_items: sugar is a process model, not granular physics: the mound, the stream and the sugar in the jar are drawn from the task's grams; the sugar in the jar stays a level cylinder in the jar's frame while it tilts
the stir dissolves the mound fully after the two turns (appearance only); the tea's colour does not change
the jar's 120 g glass mass plus its sugar is a fixed 200 g rigid body
